Mara ducked into the relay room with rain still ticking against the outer housing. She thumbed the restart switch. The carrier lamp stayed dark.

She opened the cabinet and worked down the relay stack until the gap caught her eye. The fuse socket was empty. Its ceramic clips still held a trace of warmth.

Someone had pulled the fuse only minutes ago.

Mara looked back to the dead carrier lamp. Whatever else had happened, the beacon was not coming back until that fuse was replaced.

Mara ducked into the relay room with rain ticking against the outer housing. She thumbed the restart switch. The carrier lamp stayed dark.

She opened the relay cabinet and worked down the stack one component at a time. At the fuse block, she stopped. The socket was empty.

That was enough to explain the dead carrier. Without the relay fuse, K-17 could not transmit.

Mara kept her eyes on the open cabinet. The fault was clear. Who had left it that way was not.
